pinterest.title: Notice of Intended Marriage Explained Step by Step
pinterest.description: Marrying in Australia? A Notice of Intended Marriage (NOIM) is the written notice every couple gives their authorised marriage celebrant. As at November 2026, it must reach your celebrant at least one month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. Our step by step guide covers the form, who can witness it, the documents you need and what changes if you marry legally abroad.

pinterest.title: When to Lodge Your Notice of Intended Marriage: The 1 to 18 Month Window
pinterest.description: Your NOIM can reach your celebrant up to 18 months before the wedding, and no later than one month before. Treat one month as a floor, not a target: your celebrant also needs to meet each of you separately and in person. With less than a month to go, a prescribed authority may approve a shorter notice on grounds such as travel commitments or medical reasons. Read the full guide.

pinterest.title: Notice of Intended Marriage Documents Checklist
pinterest.description: Alongside your Notice of Intended Marriage, your authorised celebrant will ask for evidence of your date and place of birth, evidence of your identity, proof that any previous marriage has ended, and a separate in-person meeting with each of you. Keep the originals together in one folder. Planning a destination wedding? Our guide explains which paperwork applies.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Marrying in Australia, or marrying here and celebrating overseas? Your first piece of paperwork is the Notice of Intended Marriage, or NOIM.

It is the written notice every couple gives the authorised celebrant who will marry them. As at November 2026, it must reach your celebrant at least one month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. Without it, the marriage cannot go ahead.

The order is simple: get the official form from the Attorney-General's Department, sign it in front of an authorised witness, give it to your celebrant, then provide your documents. Since 12 June 2024 it can be witnessed in person or by audio-visual link, but not online if you sign overseas.

Running short on time? With less than one month to go, you may still marry if a prescribed authority approves it, on grounds such as travel commitments, celebration arrangements or medical reasons. Start with your celebrant, and treat it as a fallback, not a plan.

Planning to marry legally abroad instead? The NOIM does not come into it. You follow the destination's own rules, and some countries ask for a Certificate of No Impediment.

Our new guide walks through the form, the witnessing rules, the documents and which paperwork applies to destination couples.

The NOIM, the legal date and any local paperwork stay with you and your celebrant or the local authority. The celebration is where we come in. Send us a message and your Wedded Advisor, one person from start to finish, will plan the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, in your time zone. Full guide at the link in our bio.
